args: I need to crunch some data on a first aid form. We released a new first aid form this season, which presents questions to members based on what they responded to. This was an upgrade from a very basic form that we previously used. In the OneDrive inbox there is a First Aid Form Data Spreadsheet. One of my colleagues has done some formula crunching. I would like you to ultra examine this data. As if you were a professional data scientist, come in to give us insights. There are a few things we want to explore: 1.Areas where the form has given us clarity on things we could get clarity on from the previous version of the form. 2. Any trends in our first aid presentations. 3. Any areas of the form that give us useful insights. James has picket time from opening to completion, a couple of questions sets that often get answered poorly. This will help us evaluate both the effectiveness of the form and areas we may need to train our members. What I would like is insights that I can put into a report to present to executives and other states to show the success of our first aid form upgrade. Both from a user satisfaction point of view, but also a First Aid Practice point of view. Think of a conference presentation. What data can I use to wow people. Be extrmely thorough, applying the highest level of data science skills. Do not make assumptions or inferrences, only go off the data in that spreadsheet. Do not stop until you have achieved this outcome.
